content.text: Hello! Today, we will learn about **Balanced Binary Trees**. We already saw how tree shapes affect search time. Now, we will formalize what a balanced tree is and why it guarantees optimal search performance!
1. What is a Balanced Binary Tree?
A binary tree is considered **height-balanced** if, for every node in the tree, the height of its left and right subtrees differs by **at most 1**.

Mathematically, for every node:
**| Height(Left) - Height(Right) | ≤ 1**

Imagine kids playing on a seesaw. If one side has a heavy weight and the other side is empty, the seesaw crashes down to one side. In tree terms, that side is too 'heavy' (tall). A balanced tree keeps the left and right subtrees nearly equal in height, making it look balanced.

In a balanced tree containing $N$ elements, the height is guaranteed to be $O(\log N)$. This means searching, insertion, and deletion will all take $O(\log N)$ time, which is incredibly fast! Without balance, search time degrades to $O(N)$.
